Also known as: Earnings Before Interest and Tax; Earnings Before Interest and Taxes
Definition: Profit from normal business operations, before accounting for interest on debt or taxes.
Profit from operations before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization are subtracted -- a common way to compare underlying profitability across companies.
Similar to EBITDA but before amortization only (depreciation is still included).
What's left of revenue after subtracting the direct cost of producing what was sold.
Total sales after subtracting things like returns, discounts, and allowances.

Also known as: Cost of Goods Sold; Cost of Sales
Definition: The direct cost of producing whatever was actually sold in the period.
The running total from the start of the fiscal year up to now.
The running total from the start of the current month up to now.
The running total from the start of the current quarter up to now.
A comparison of a figure against the same period one year earlier.
Money owed to the company by customers who haven't paid their invoices yet.
Money the company owes to its own suppliers that hasn't been paid yet.
On average, how many days it takes to collect payment after a sale is made.
Money spent on long-term assets like equipment, buildings, or major upgrades.
The day-to-day costs of running the business, outside of what's directly tied to producing goods sold.
The difference between an actual result and what was planned or budgeted.
How much value or profit was gained relative to what was spent.
A financial statement showing revenue, costs, and resulting profit or loss over a period.
The point where revenue exactly covers costs -- no profit, no loss.
Shared or indirect costs (like admin or overhead) distributed across departments, products, or business units according to a set rule.
A projection of a future figure, based on current trends, plans, or orders already in hand.
The total value of goods or services sold to customers in a period, before any costs are deducted.

Also known as: Net Profit; Net Income; Net Earnings
Definition: What is left of revenue after all costs, interest and taxes have been deducted.
Profit from the core business, after operating costs but before interest and taxes.
Operating profit (EBIT) as a share of revenue, showing how much of each unit of sales is left after operating costs.
Net profit shown as a percentage of revenue, which is how much of each unit of sales is left as profit after all costs.
EBITDA shown as a percentage of revenue, which shows how much operating profit before depreciation and amortisation is made from each unit of sales.
Money spent to run the business or produce goods and services.
The planned amount of revenue or spending for a period, set in advance to compare actual results against.
The figure that really happened in the period, as opposed to the budget, target or forecast.
The net amount of cash moving into and out of the business in a period.
Cash generated by operations after paying for the investments needed to keep the business running and growing.
Current assets minus current liabilities: the short-term funds available to run day-to-day operations.
Net profit as a share of shareholders' equity, showing how well owners' money is being used to generate profit.
Net profit as a share of total assets, showing how well assets are used to generate profit.
Operating profit as a share of the capital used in the business.

Also known as: Gross Margin %; Gross Profit Margin; GP Margin
Definition: The gross profit shown as a percentage of revenue, which is the share of each sale left after the direct cost of the goods or service.
The contribution, which is sales less variable costs, shown as a percentage of sales.
Costs of running the business that are not tied directly to making a product or delivering a service, such as rent, admin and management salaries.
Costs that stay the same however much is produced or sold, such as rent and salaries.
Costs that rise and fall with how much is produced or sold, such as materials and packaging.

Also known as: Direct Costs of Sales; Prime Cost
Definition: A cost that can be traced straight to a product or service, such as materials and the labour used to make it.

Also known as: Standard Costing; Standard Cost per Unit
Definition: The cost that was planned for making a unit, used as a yardstick to compare with what was actually spent.

Also known as: Cost Overrun; Expense Variance; Spend Variance
Definition: The difference between what was planned to be spent and what was actually spent.
The difference between planned and actual revenue.
The part of a change in results that comes from selling or buying at a different price than planned.
The part of a change in results that comes from selling or using more or fewer units than planned.

Also known as: Product Mix Variance; Sales Mix Variance
Definition: The part of a change in results that comes from selling a different blend of products than planned.

Also known as: Forecast vs Actual; Forecast Error Finance
Definition: The difference between the forecast and the actual result.

Also known as: Budget Variance Percent; Over Under Budget Percent
Definition: The difference between actual and budget shown as a percentage of the budget.

Also known as: Depreciation Expense; Depreciation and Amortisation; D&A
Definition: The way the cost of a physical asset is spread over the years it is used, shown as a yearly charge in the accounts.
The way the cost of an intangible asset, such as software or a licence, is spread over the years it is used.

Also known as: Finance Cost; Interest Cost; Interest Paid
Definition: The cost of borrowing, such as interest paid on loans, in a period.

Also known as: Interest Coverage Ratio; Times Interest Earned; TIE
Definition: How many times the operating profit covers the interest due. A higher figure means interest is easier to pay.

Also known as: PBT; Pre-Tax Profit; Earnings Before Tax
Definition: The profit made before income tax is taken off.
The profit left after income tax has been taken off.
The tax charge shown as a percentage of profit before tax.

Also known as: Income Tax Expense; Tax Charge; Tax Provision
Definition: The income tax charged against profit in a period.
The part of profit paid out to shareholders.
The profits that have been kept in the business over time instead of paid out as dividends.
A statement showing what the business owns, what it owes and the owners' stake at one point in time.
Everything the business owns that has value, such as cash, stock, equipment and money owed by customers.
Assets expected to be turned into cash within a year, such as cash, receivables and stock.

Also known as: Non-Current Assets; PPE Assets; Property Plant and Equipment
Definition: Long-term assets used in the business, such as buildings and machines.

Also known as: Short-Term Liabilities; Short-Term Debts; Creditors Due Within a Year
Definition: Amounts the business must pay within a year, such as supplier bills and short loans.
Everything the business owes, such as loans, supplier bills and other obligations.

Also known as: Shareholders' Equity; Owners' Equity; Net Assets
Definition: The owners' stake in the business, which is its assets minus its liabilities.
The total borrowings minus cash, showing how much debt would remain if cash were used to repay it.

Also known as: Debt Equity Ratio; Gearing Ratio; Leverage
Definition: The borrowings shown against the owners' stake. A higher figure means the business relies more on borrowed money.
How many years of EBITDA it would take to repay the net debt.
The current assets divided by the current liabilities, showing whether short-term bills can be paid.

Also known as: Acid Test; Acid Test Ratio; Liquid Ratio
Definition: The current assets, without stock, divided by the current liabilities. It is a stricter test of whether short-term bills can be paid.

Also known as: Cash on Hand; Cash and Equivalents; Closing Cash
Definition: The cash held by the business at a point in time.

Also known as: Cash from Operations; Cash Flow from Operating Activities; CFO
Definition: The cash the business generates from its normal day-to-day activities.
The average number of days the business takes to pay its suppliers.

Also known as: Stock Days; Inventory Days; Days in Inventory
Definition: The average number of days stock is held before it is sold.

Also known as: AR Ageing; Debtors Ageing; Aged Debtors
Definition: A breakdown of money owed by customers by how long it has been unpaid, such as 0 to 30 days or over 90 days.

Also known as: Bad Debt Expense; Doubtful Debts; Write-Offs Receivables
Definition: Money owed by customers that is not expected to be paid.
How much of the money that could have been collected in a period was actually collected.

Also known as: Invoices Raised; Number of Invoices; Invoices Issued
Definition: The number of invoices raised in a period.

Also known as: Credit Notes Issued; Credits Issued; Sales Credits
Definition: A document that reduces what a customer owes, usually after a return or a billing error.

Also known as: Accrued Expenses; Accrued Liabilities; Accrued Income
Definition: Costs or income that belong to a period but have not yet been paid or received.
Payments made in advance for goods or services to be received in a later period.

Also known as: Unearned Revenue; Contract Liabilities; Deferred Income
Definition: Money received from customers for goods or services that have not yet been delivered.

Also known as: Recognised Revenue; Recognized Revenue; Revenue Recognized
Definition: Counting revenue in the accounts in the period when it is earned, not necessarily when the money is received.
Transactions or balances between two companies in the same group, which are removed when group figures are put together.

Also known as: FX Rate; Currency Rate; Forex Rate
Definition: The price of one currency in terms of another, used to convert foreign amounts.

Also known as: FX Gain Loss; Currency Gain or Loss; Exchange Difference
Definition: The gain or loss that arises because exchange rates changed between the time of a transaction and the time it was settled or reported.

Also known as: Constant FX; Currency Neutral; Excluding FX
Definition: Results restated at a fixed exchange rate so that growth is not affected by currency movements.
The operating profit after tax shown as a percentage of the capital invested in the business.
The profit shown as a percentage of the capital used to produce it.
The profit left after charging for the cost of all the capital used, showing whether the business created real value.
The value today of the cash a project will bring in, minus its cost, with future cash discounted for the time it takes to arrive.
The yearly return rate at which a project's future cash would exactly repay what was invested.

Also known as: Payback Time; Simple Payback; Investment Payback
Definition: The time taken for a project's cash inflows to pay back the amount invested.
The average rate the business pays to fund itself through a mix of debt and equity.

Also known as: Quality of Earnings; Cash Conversion of Profit
Definition: How closely the reported profit matches real cash and whether it can be repeated, rather than coming from one-off items.

Also known as: Exceptional Items; Non-Recurring Items; Adjusting Items
Definition: Income or costs that are unusual and not expected to repeat, which are often shown separately to give a clearer view of the normal result.

Also known as: Underlying EBITDA; Normalised EBITDA; Normalized EBITDA
Definition: EBITDA after removing one-off or unusual items so that it shows the ongoing performance.

Also known as: GP per Head; Gross Profit per FTE
Definition: The gross profit divided by the number of employees.

Also known as: Employee Cost per Head; Staff Cost per FTE
Definition: The cost of employing people divided by the number of employees.

Also known as: Cost Savings Finance; Cost Out; Savings Programme
Definition: The amount by which costs have been cut compared with a baseline.

Also known as: O2C; Order to Cash; Order-to-Cash Cycle Time
Definition: The time from receiving a customer order to collecting the money for it.

Also known as: Close Days; Financial Close Cycle; Days to Close
Definition: The number of working days needed after the month ends to finish and approve the accounts.

Also known as: Manual Journals; Journal Count; Adjusting Entries
Definition: The number of entries made directly to the accounting records, where manual ones carry a higher risk of error.

Also known as: Account Reconciliation; Bank Reconciliation; Reconciled Accounts
Definition: Checking that two sets of records, such as the bank statement and the accounts, agree and explaining any differences.

Also known as: Audit Differences; Proposed Adjustments; Audit Findings Finance
Definition: Changes to the accounts that the auditors asked for after finding errors.
